newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia's Gorenjska, UBK banks in merger talks.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia's Gorenjska, UBK banks in merger talks.

text.p: Slovenian banks Gorenjska banka and UBK said on Thursday they were in negotiations about a possible merger but declined to give a timeframe for the potential tie-up.
"If we join Gorenjska banka, both banks would become much stronger," UBK chief executive Matjaz Kastrun told Reuters.

Gorenjska banka's chief executive Zlatko Kavcic declined to comment on the talks. "We've had many talks about business reorganisation and cooperation with different banks, but it is still too early to say when or whether anything will happen."

However, he said Gorenjska banka, whose retail market share rose to 4.5 percent this year from four percent in 1995, could benefit from a possible merger mostly by further increasing its market share and business capacity.
A merger could also result in lower operating costs and improvement in the banks' personnel structure, he said.
Total assets of Gorenjska rose to 65.9 billion tolars ($477.5 million) at the end of last year from 54.5 billion in 1994, while UBK's balance sheet rose to 13.9 billion tolars from 10.4 billion.
